lines: Mr Anderson shut the door. Mr Anderson did not look up.
Then the master called the imp, and the master laughed.
rationale: a bundled title and a dual-use word the book capitalises and not: both are recurring terms the run keeps one rendering for

lines: The pupils gathered in the Great Hall before dinner.
They crossed the great hall slowly, and the hall was cold; an old man sat by the old fire.
Nobody liked the Old Bailey, and the old courts were grim.
rationale: Great Hall and Old Bailey are names for the glossary; their words great, hall and old are generic and must not become recurring terms (the real run proposed them)

lines: Mr Anderson shut the door. Mr Anderson did not look up.
The pupils gathered in the Great Hall before dinner.
He was tried at the Old Bailey in the spring, and the Old Bailey was full.
rationale: the name scan keeps the person without the title and the two-word places whole
